policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And the chief priests' renders a simple connective; te and de are both carried by 'and' and the English cannot tell them apart.
ASV reads plural 'the chief priests', matching hoi archiereis; the RP singular ho archiereus would give 'the high priest'.
ASV 'was kept in charge at Caesarea' renders the phrase locatively, but in Koine eis with a verb of custody is regularly rendered 'at'; the preposition is not distinguished by the English.
r00 and r01 differ only in punctuation, which no translation can show; r02 differs only in Greek word order, and ASV 'that are of power among you, saith he' reorders for English idiom in either case.
ASV 'if there is anything amiss in the man' renders atopon by 'amiss'; the RP reading has no such word (and would give 'this man').
ASV 'not more than eight or ten days' renders ou pleious okto with both the negative comparative and the numeral; r01 lacks 'eight' and r02 lacks 'not more than'.
ASV 'stood round about him' supplies the object pronoun of periestesan, answering to auton, which RP omits.
ASV reads 'bringing against him many and grievous charges'; the RP reading names Paul (kata tou Paulou), which the ASV would have rendered 'against Paul' rather than 'against him'.
ASV 'while Paul said in his defence' names Paul in the genitive absolute, matching tou Paulou apologoumenou; the RP reading has only the pronoun autou.
The readings differ only in Greek word order; ASV 'desiring to gain favor with the Jews' renders the same words either way.
ASV 'there be judged' is a bare passive infinitive that shows no aspect; aorist krithenai and present krinesthai are rendered alike.
The readings differ only in the position of hestos; ASV 'I am standing before Caesar's judgment-seat' follows English order and does not distinguish them.
ASV 'have I done no wrong' can render either the aorist edikesa or the perfect edikeka; the English present-perfect does not fix the Greek tense here.
ASV 'If then I am a wrong-doer' renders oun by 'then'; RP's gar would have been rendered 'for'.
ASV 'as they tarried there many days' has a plural subject, matching plural dietribon against RP's singular dietriben ('as he tarried').
ASV 'asking for sentence against him' renders katadiken, the word for a condemnatory sentence; the ASV renders bare dike elsewhere as justice or punishment, not 'sentence'.
ASV 'to give up any man, before that the accused have the accusers face to face' has no rendering of the RP addition eis apoleian ('unto destruction').
ASV 'When therefore they were come together here' supplies 'they' as the subject of the genitive absolute, which English requires whether or not auton stands in the Greek.
ASV 'they brought no charge' renders pheron and the compound epepheron alike; the prefix leaves no English trace.
The readings differ only in the order of ego and hypenooun; ASV 'as I supposed' is the same either way.
ASV 'no charge of such evil things as I supposed' renders poneron by 'evil things', which RP omits.
ASV 'how to inquire concerning these things' is plural, matching touton; RP's singular toutou would give 'concerning this matter'.
ASV renders both the Hellenised Hierosolyma and the Semitic Ierousalem as 'Jerusalem'; the spelling is invisible in English.
ASV 'till I should send him to Caesar' renders simple pempso and compound anapempso alike; 'send up' is not distinguished.

The base leaves the verb of speaking elliptical, so ASV 'And Agrippa said unto Festus' requires 'said' in English whether or not ephe stands in the Greek. The mapped note is an alternative_rendering about 'could wish' and decides nothing.
ASV gives 'To-morrow, saith he, thou shalt hear him' with no rendering of RP's ho de, which the ASV renders 'And he' or 'But he' wherever it stands; only phesin ('saith he') is represented.
The variant is the presence of the article tois with 'chief captains'; ASV 'with the chief captains' shows no difference either way.
ASV 'and the principal men of the city' would read the same with or without the participle ousin, which English idiom absorbs.
ASV 'all men who are here present' renders hapan and pan identically; the strengthened form has no separate English.
ASV 'all the multitude of the Jews made suit to me' takes a collective subject whose English verb is the same for the plural enetychon and the singular enetychen.
ASV 'crying that he ought not to live any longer' renders boontes and the compound epiboontes alike.
The readings differ only in the order of auton and zen; ASV 'that he ought not to live any longer' follows English order.

ASV 'But I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death: and ... I determined to send him' makes 'I found' a finite verb coordinate with 'I determined', matching the indicative katelabomen; RP's participle katalabomenos would give 'when I found' subordinated to the one main verb.
The readings differ only in the order of auton and thanatou; ASV 'he had committed nothing worthy of death' is the same either way.
ASV 'and as he himself appealed to the emperor' has one 'and', which the de of the clause already accounts for; the added kai leaves no separate English trace.
ASV 'I determined to send him' needs an English object for 'send' whether or not auton stands in the Greek, so the pronoun does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'I have no certain thing to write unto my lord' renders the object infinitive the same way for grapso and grapsai.
